proposal: Refuse acceptance while the calibration ledger measures SYSTEMATICALLY_OVERCONFIDENT (canonical/runtime/raw_goal_trace_acceptance_v1.verify + self_prediction_calibration_v1.gate)
decisive_question: Does refusing acceptance while overconfident make the system less overconfident?
counterexamples: The gate changes what is accepted, not what is predicted. A system can keep claiming 0.85 and be refused forever; the refusal removes the evidence it would need to become calibrated, so the gate can freeze the very state it objects to.
The measurement is only as independent as the inspectors. Predictions settled by a weak inspector produce a confident, wrong score, and the gate then refuses on the strength of a bad measurement.

The refusal covers acceptance, not action. Work still executes, artifacts are still written; only the acceptance verdict is withheld. Anything downstream that reads the artifact without consulting the acceptance path is unaffected.

Failed attempts settle as failures rather than staying unrecorded only where an inspector exists; a step with no inspector settles as a failure, which is right, but it also means coverage gaps push the ledger down rather than being held out.

measured.empty_ledger: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, gate does not refuse and reports that it ran

implication: The score now has a consequence, which is the difference between a dashboard and a self-model. It is a consequence, not a correction: nothing here makes the system better at predicting itself, and a refusal can persist indefinitely. The first counterexample is the one to watch -- a gate that blocks the evidence needed to escape it is a trap, and only an external hard-task slice avoids it.
what_would_closes_it: Not applicable as stated: closing it requires the scheduler step (B4) that forces the hard slice, so the system can accumulate honest hard-case evidence while refused.
